He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before making his professional debut in the NBL for the [[Sydney Kings]] in 2017. After two seasons in the [[NBA G League]] and making his [[NBA]] debut for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 2019, Humphries joined the Adelaide 36ers in 2020. He played two seasons for the 36ers before joining [[Melbourne United]] for a season, and then re-joining the 36ers in 2023. Humphries is the first NBL player to [[Coming out|come out as gay]]. He is also a singer and cabaret performer, performing at the [[Adelaide Fringe]] in 2024 and 2025. ==Early life and career== Isaac Bradley Humphries was born on 5 January 1998{{cite web | title=Isaac Bradley Humphries (Australia) | website=FIBA Basketball | url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/205891-isaac-bradley-humphries | access-date=23 January 2025}} in the [[Sydney]] suburb of [[Caringbah]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/109830/sid/6224/tid/239/_/2014_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|title=Isaac Humphries|work=FIBA.com|access-date=27 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911161537/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/109830/sid/6224/tid/239/_/2014_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-date=11 September 2017}} He grew up in [[Cronulla]], where the predominant culture was [[Surf culture|surfing and beach]]. He was a musical child, playing [[violin]] at four, [[trumpet]] the following year, and piano later. He was also a gifted singer, performing on stages around Sydney before he started playing basketball.{{cite interview| first=Isaac |last=Humphries| title=Meet our 2024 Ambassador | website=[[Adelaide Humphries attended [[Scots College (Sydney)|Scots College]] in [[Sydney]], where he reached {{cvt|7|ft}} in height by the time he was 16.{{cite web | last=Gaskin | first=Lee | title=Basketball player Isaac Humphries has the world at his feet | website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] | date=27 January 2014 | I was terrified' | website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] | date=11 February 2023 | url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/life-changes-tomorrow-what-happened-when-pro-basketball-s-isaac-humphries-came-out-20221205-p5c3sh.html | access-date=24 January 2025| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230212063340/https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/life-changes-tomorrow-what-happened-when-pro-basketball-s-isaac-humphries-came-out-20221205-p5c3sh.html| archive-date=12 Feb 2023|url-status=live}} In 2014, Humphries moved to [[Canberra]] to attend the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] (AIS) and play for the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL). In nine SEABL games, he averaged 7.8 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Isaac Humphries, Basketball Player, News, Stats - australiabasket |url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Isaac-Humphries/328732 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=8 March 2025 |url-access=subscription}} During his time at the AIS, he played around the world with the [[Australia men's national under-17 basketball team|national under-17s team]]. ==College career== [[File:Isaac-Humphries.jpg|thumb|right|Humphries with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] in 2016]] Humphries took his game to the United States in December 2014{{Cite news|url=http://www.theleader.com.au/story/3363762/sutherland-sharks-basketball-association-junior-issac-humphries-us-dream/|title=Sutherland Sharks Basketball Association junior Issac Humphries' US dream|last=Haigh|first=Paul|date=23 September 2015|work=St George & Sutherland Shire Leader|access-date=20 May 2017|url-access=registration}} to play prep ball at [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]].{{Cite news|url=http://hoopshype.ca/7-footer-humphries-joins-four-canadians-la-lumiere/|title=7-Footer Humphries Joins Four Canadians At La Lumiere - Hoops Hype Canada {{!}} Canadian Basketball News|date=14 December 2014|work=Hoops Hype Canada {{!}} Canadian Basketball News|access-date=20 May 2017|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220184124/http://hoopshype.ca/7-footer-humphries-joins-four-canadians-la-lumiere/|archive-date=20 February 2015|url-status=dead}} Humphries enrolled at the [[University of Kentucky]], where he saw action in 23 games as a freshman with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Wildcats]] in 2015–16. Coming off the bench in all but one game, he averaged 1.9 points and 2.4 rebounds in 9.1 minutes per contest.{{Cite news|url=http://kty-oas-web-prod.slabs-cloud.com/page/m-baskbl_team_stats_2015-2016|title=2015-16 Men's Basketball Team Stats - UK Wildcats|work=University of Kentucky {{!}} Official Athletics {{S-end}} ==Music career== While playing basketball in the US, Humphries occasionally sang the [[American national anthem]] before basketball matches, and for charity events. He restarted his music career after some years immersed in basketball, during which time he started learning new instruments that he could play anywhere. {{as of|2024}} he was continuing the two careers in parallel, performing as well as writing and releasing music. In that year, he was an ambassador for the [[Adelaide Fringe]], as well as performing a show called ''Unearthed''. It was so named because it focused on sharing personal moments and songs that helped him "unearth" who he became. The show included original songs as well as [[cover version]]s, which he sings in his [[tenor]] voice.{{cite interview| first=Isaac |last=Humphries| title=Meet 4 fabulous Adelaide Fringe Ambassadors | website=Seniors Card | date=6 February 2024 | url=https://www.seniorscard.sa.gov.au/weekendplus/lifestyle/meet-4-fabulous-adelaide-fringe-ambassadors | access-date=24 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241024215041/https://www.seniorscard.sa.gov.au/weekendplus/lifestyle/meet-4-fabulous-adelaide-fringe-ambassadors| archive-date= 24 Oct 2024| url-status=live}} The season sold out.{{cite web | title=Isaac Humphries | website=[[Adelaide Fringe]] | url=https://adelaidefringe.com.au/fringetix/isaac-humphries-more-of-me-af2025 | access-date=24 January 2025}} For the 2025 Adelaide Fringe, Humphries performs his show called ''More of Me''. ==Personal life== On 16 November 2022, Humphries [[Coming out|came out]] as [[Gay men|gay]].{{Cite web |title=Former Kentucky center, Melbourne United star Isaac Humphries comes out publicly as gay |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/former-kentucky-center-melbourne-united-star-isaac-humphries-comes-out-publicly-as-gay-233046180.html |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=sports.yahoo.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2023-01-26 |title=NBL’s first openly gay player Isaac Humphries ‘disappointed’ by Cairns rejection of Pride jersey |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2023/jan/27/nbls-first-openly-gay-player-isaac-humphries-disappointed-by-cairns-rejection-of-pride-jersey |access-date=2023-08-15 |issn=0261-3077}} The announcement saw Humphries become the only active openly gay male professional basketball player in a top-tier league anywhere in the world. He also became the first ever Australian male basketball player and first player in the NBL to be openly gay.{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/11/15/opinions/gay-australian-basketball-player-isaac-humphries/index.html|title=Opinion: Why Australia's elite basketballer is ready to tell the world he is gay|work=cnn.com|date=15 November 2022|access-date=16 November 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.melbourneutd.com.au/news/melbourne-united-supports-and-celebrates-isaac-humphries-courageous-decision|title=Melbourne United supports and celebrates Isaac Humphries' courageous decision|work=melbourneutd.com.au|date=16 November 2022|access-date=16 November 2022}} He said that he had struggled with his sexuality and contemplated suicide, but ultimately decided that he would be happier to be open about it with his teammates.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-16 |title=‘Courageous’: NBL star comes out to teammates as first openly gay player as NBA reacts |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-2022-isaac-humphries-comes-out-as-gay-announcement-video-tried-to-take-his-own-life-first-nbl-player-basketball/news-story/98d91fc670f898742183023be75299fd |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=Fox Sports |language=en}} He posted a video online, which was shared widely, including by [[Lauren Jackson]], [[Dylan Alcott]], and [[Andrew Gaze]]. By February 2023 it had garnered around 10 million views, with mostly positive responses, including messages from [[Tones and I]] and [[Dannii Minogue]]. However, although the NBA sent a message of solidarity, not a single active NBA player showed support. Humphries has a tattoo on his arm reading "silence is loud", referring to his depression.
